newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-JONES RESIGNS AS DERBYSHIRE CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JONES RESIGNS AS DERBYSHIRE CAPTAIN.

text.p: Dean Jones quit as Derbyshire captain and overseas player on Thursday, with dressing room unrest and poor performances thought to be behind the shock decision.

"It's with deepest regret that I have informed Derbyshire CCC (County Cricket Club) that I am resigning as captain and overseas professional forthwith," the former Australian test batsman said in a statement.
Jones, who last season led his team to second place in the county championship, blamed a lack of support from senior players for the decision which he described as one of the toughest in his career.
"Over the past month a few senior players have failed to give me any support in my endeavours to carry on the Derbyshire CCC success from last year," he said.
"These players have difficulty in coming to terms with the fundamentals that bring success."
Derbyshire currently lie second bottom in the 18-team championship.
County chairman Mike Horton, who reluctantly accepted the resignation, said the committee wished Jones every success for the future.
Stewart Edwards, secretary and general manager at the club, said: "We are obviously very disappointed that Dean has decided to resign the captaincy and return to Australia."
Phillip DeFreitas, the current vice-captain, has been appointed skipper for the next two matches, starting with Thursday's game against Warwickshire at Edgbaston.
